interactions.summary: Students test two bad answers to the free-will question, and Jiang pushes both away: God does not borrow free will through humans, and free will cannot be explained as a laboratory experiment where God watches reactions.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led rejection of student trial models

interactions.summary: A student reframes free will as the needed contrast that makes the journey toward God meaningful, and Jiang again presses on whether that still reduces God to a maze-maker running an experiment.
A student offers the imago-dei answer that humans receive agency because they are made in God's image, and Jiang treats it as still incomplete by asking why God wants humans to have agency at all.

speaker_notes.note: This segment interleaves Jiang's short prompts with the student's answer, but the argumentative point is clear enough to treat it as one exchange.

claims.claim: Jiang rejects the proposal that God somehow lacks free will and exercises it through human beings, calling that idea nonsensical because God is God.
Jiang rejects any account of free will that turns creation into an experiment where God watches human reactions like a scientist watching mice in a lab.

The class proposes that the possibility of not reaching God creates the contrast that makes the journey toward God meaningful, but Jiang keeps that explanation under pressure rather than accepting it as final.
A more promising answer in this packet is that humans have agency because they are made in God's image, though Jiang explicitly treats that as requiring a deeper explanation.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang refuses to let God become a scientist experimenting on mice.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we're like mice in a lab
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The image preserves the force of Jiang's refusal to explain freedom by reducing creation to divine experimentation.

signature_moments.moment: The strongest student answer is that humans have agency because they are made in God's image.
signature_moments.source_phrase: God made man in his own image
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's main constructive line even though Jiang keeps probing beyond it.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The capacity for real choice that the student connects to being made in God's image and that Jiang treats as central enough to require further grounding.
A rejected model of creation in which God sets up free will merely to observe outcomes, like a scientist testing mice in a maze.

chronology_notes.note: Rather than resolving why God gives free will, this packet clears away several weak explanations and narrows the discussion toward image, agency, and a still-unanswered deeper rationale.

uncertainty_notes.note: The contrast-based answer is presented as a student's provisional attempt and should be carried forward as live classroom pressure rather than as Jiang's final position.
